prompt: For \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+5}\), what is the slope of the secant through inputs \(4\) and \(4+h\), before taking the limit? Assume \(h\ne0\) and \(4+h\) is in the domain.
why: Multiply \((\sqrt{9+h}-3)/h\) by its conjugate over itself. The new numerator is \(h\), which cancels.

prompt: The graph of \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+5}\) passes through \((4,3)\) with tangent slope \(1/6\). Where does that tangent cross the horizontal axis?
why: Rationalizing the difference quotient gives slope \(1/6\) at \((4,3)\). Set \(0-3=(x-4)/6\) and solve.

prompt: Set \(f(x)=(x+1)^2\) for \(x\ne-1\) and \(f(-1)=1\). As \(h\) tends to zero from the left and right, respectively, what are the limits of \([f(-1+h)-f(-1)]/h\)?
why: For \(h\ne0\) the quotient is \((h^2-1)/h=h-1/h\). Its one-sided limits have opposite signs.

prompt: At \(x=3\), \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+6}\) has value \(3\) and tangent slope \(1/6\). Use this tangent to estimate \(f(3.12)\).
why: The point is \((3,3)\) and the derivative there is \(1/6\). The tangent predicts an increase of \(0.12/6=0.02\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=3x-x^2\), the derivative is \(3-2x\). The secant over \([a,a+h]\), where \(h>0\), has slope \(3-2a-h\). At which input is the tangent parallel to that secant?
why: Differentiate to get \(f'(c)=3-2c\). Equating the two slopes gives \(2c=2a+h\).

prompt: A particle travels for \(0\le t\le4\) with velocity \(v(t)=3(t-1)(t-3)\) and acceleration \(a(t)=6(t-2)\). On which open intervals does its speed increase?
why: Velocity is \(3(t-1)(t-3)\) and acceleration is \(6(t-2)\). Their signs agree precisely on \((1,2)\) and \((3,4)\).

prompt: A particle has \(v(t)=3(t-1)(t-3)\) and \(a(t)=6(t-2)\). Just before and just after \(t=2\), how do direction and speed change?
choices: It keeps moving in the negative direction. Its speed changes from increasing to decreasing.
It keeps moving in the negative direction. Its speed changes from decreasing to increasing.
It reverses into the positive direction. Its speed is zero at the turn.
It keeps moving in the positive direction. Its speed changes from increasing to decreasing.
why: Velocity is \(-3\) at \(t=2\) and stays negative nearby. Acceleration changes from negative to positive, so speed has a local maximum.

prompt: A ball is released at height \(96\) feet and hits the ground \(2\) seconds later. Its velocity in feet per second is \(v(t)=-16-32t\). What are its average velocity over the flight and its velocity just before impact, respectively?
why: The height change divided by elapsed time is \(-96/2=-48\) ft/s. Substituting \(t=2\) in the velocity gives \(-16-64=-80\) ft/s.

prompt: A car is at position \(s(t)=t^2-2t-3\) feet at time \(t\ge0\) seconds. Which list gives every time when \(s=-3\) ft and the signed velocity at each time?
choices: \(0\) s at \(2\) ft/s and \(2\) s at \(2\) ft/s
why: Set \(t^2-2t=0\) to find both admissible times. Substituting each into \(2t-2\) gives opposite velocities.

prompt: A particle moves during \(0<t<5\) with velocity \(-3(t-2)(t-4)\) and acceleration \(6(3-t)\). When is it both moving left and speeding up?
why: Moving left and speeding up requires both \(v=-3(t-2)(t-4)<0\) and \(a=-6(t-3)<0\). Only \((4,5)\) satisfies both.

prompt: A particle has velocity \(v(t)=-3(t-2)(t-4)\) and acceleration \(a(t)=6(3-t)\) for \(0<t<5\). At which instants does it reverse direction? When does acceleration change sign without a reversal?
choices: Reversals at \(2,4\); acceleration changes sign at \(3\).
Reversal at \(3\); acceleration changes sign at \(2,4\).
Reversals at \(2,3,4\); acceleration never changes sign.
Reversal at \(4\) only; acceleration changes sign at \(2\).
why: Velocity is \(-3(t-2)(t-4)\) and changes sign at both roots. Acceleration vanishes at \(3\), where velocity is positive.

prompt: For \(f(x)=\lvert x\rvert\), the secant joining \(-h\) to \(h\) has slope zero for every \(h>0\). Why does this fail to give \(f'(0)=0\)?
choices: The secants from \(0\) to \(h\) and from \(0\) to \(-h\) have different limiting slopes.
The derivative is zero because all symmetric secants are horizontal.
The derivative is one because the graph lies above the horizontal axis.
The derivative fails because the function is discontinuous at zero.
why: The derivative requires the difference quotient based at \(0\). It equals \(1\) on the right and \(-1\) on the left, while the symmetric quotient always compares equal heights.

prompt: For \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+5}\), the secant from \(4\) to \(4+h\) has slope \(1/(\sqrt{9+h}+3)\) for \(h\ne0\) and \(h\ge-9\). Which \(h\) gives a secant slope of \(1/7\)?
why: Rationalization gives the secant slope \(1/(\sqrt{9+h}+3)\). Equate the denominator to \(7\) and solve \(\sqrt{9+h}=4\).

prompt: Suppose \(f(1)=3\) and \(f'(1)=-2\). Evaluate \(\lim_{h\to0}[f(1+h)^2-9]/h\).
why: Factor the numerator into \([f(1+h)-3][f(1+h)+3]\). The first factor divided by \(h\) tends to \(-2\). Differentiability gives continuity, so the second tends to \(6\).

prompt: A car has position \(s(t)=(t-1)^2-4\) feet at \(t\) seconds. Between \(t=0\) and \(t=3\) it turns once, at \(t=1\). What is its average speed on this interval?
why: The positions at \(0,1,3\) seconds are \(-3,-4,0\) feet. Divide the total distance \(1+4=5\) ft by \(3\) s.

prompt: For \(f(x)=3x-x^2\), what is the slope of the secant joining \((1,2)\) and \((2,2)\)?
why: Both points are at height \(2\). The change in height divided by the change in input is zero.

prompt: A secant to \(f(x)=3x-x^2\) runs from \(x=1\) to \(x=1.5\). What horizontal change belongs in the denominator of its slope?
why: Subtract the starting input from the ending input to get \(1.5-1=0.5\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=3x-x^2\), the secant slope from \(x=1\) to \(x=1+h\) simplifies to \(1-h\) when \(h\ne0\). What tangent slope does this give at \(x=1\)?
why: Let \(h\) approach zero. The limit of \(1-h\) is \(1\).

prompt: The graph of \(f(x)=mx+b\) has what instantaneous slope at \(x=2\)?
why: The slope of a line is constant. Its difference quotient is \(mh/h=m\) for \(h\ne0\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+5}\), what point on the graph do you use when forming the tangent at \(x=4\)?
why: Evaluate \(f(4)=\sqrt9=3\) and put the input first in the ordered pair.

prompt: For \(f(x)=\lvert x\rvert\), what are the right-hand and left-hand slopes at zero, in that order?
why: For \(h>0\), \(\lvert h\rvert/h=1\). For \(h<0\), \(\lvert h\rvert/h=-1\).

prompt: The first derivative of \(f(x)=3x-x^2\) is \(3-2x\). What is \(f''(x)\)?
why: The constant \(3\) differentiates to zero and the derivative of \(-2x\) is \(-2\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=3x-x^2\), which is its third derivative?
why: Its second derivative is the constant \(-2\). The derivative of a constant is zero.

prompt: A parabola has derivative \(f'(x)=3-2x\). At what input is its tangent horizontal?
why: A horizontal tangent has slope zero. Solving \(3-2x=0\) gives \(x=3/2\).

prompt: If \(y=f(x)\), which notation means the same thing as \(f'''(x)\)?
why: The superscripts in the third derivative notation count differentiations with respect to \(x\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=x^2\), the limit \(\lim_{h\to0}[(1+h)^2-1]/h\) is \(f'(a)\). Which ordered pair gives \((a,f'(a))\)?
why: The numerator is \(f(1+h)-f(1)\). Expanding gives \(2h+h^2\), so the quotient tends to \(2\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+6}\), which line is tangent to the graph at \(x=3\)?
why: The point is \((3,3)\) and rationalizing the difference quotient gives slope \(1/6\). Expand \(y-3=(x-3)/6\).

prompt: Define \(f(x)=(x+1)^2\) for \(x\ne-1\), and set \(f(-1)=1\). Why is \(f\) discontinuous at \(-1\)?
choices: The limit is \(0\) and the function value is \(1\).
The limit is \(1\) and the function value is \(0\).
The left limit is \(-1\) and the right limit is \(1\).
The function has no value at \(-1\).
why: Nearby values are \((x+1)^2\), which approach \(0\). The assigned height at \(-1\) is \(1\).

prompt: A particle has position \(s(t)=3t-t^2\) meters. What is its velocity at \(t=1\) second?
why: Differentiate to get \(v(t)=3-2t\), and substitute \(t=1\).

prompt: If velocity is \(-3\) m/s at an instant, what is the speed?
why: Speed is the magnitude of velocity, so take the absolute value.

prompt: For \(s(t)=3t-t^2\) meters, when is the particle momentarily at rest?
why: Rest means zero velocity. Solving \(3-2t=0\) gives \(t=3/2\).

prompt: At one instant a particle has velocity \(-1\) m/s and acceleration \(-2\) m/s². What is the instantaneous rate of change of its speed?
why: While velocity is negative, speed equals \(-v\). Its derivative is \(-a=2\) m/s².

prompt: The height of the ball is \(H(t)=96-16t-16t^2\) ft. Which equation finds the instant it hits the ground?
why: Ground contact specifies a height of zero. Time is measured from release, so only nonnegative roots describe this flight.

prompt: A ball has height \(H(t)=16(2-t)(t+3)\) feet after \(t\ge0\) seconds. Its velocity is \(-16-32t\) ft/s. What is its speed just before impact?
why: The nonnegative zero of \(H\) is \(t=2\). The velocity is then \(-80\) ft/s and the speed is \(80\) ft/s.

prompt: A car has position \(s(t)=t^2-2t-3\) feet at \(t\) seconds. It passes \(-3\) ft twice while \(t\ge0\). What is the later velocity minus the earlier velocity?
why: The times solve \(t(t-2)=0\). Velocities are \(2t-2=-2\) and \(2\) ft/s, so the signed change is \(4\) ft/s.

prompt: A particle has velocity \(v(t)=-3(t-2)(t-4)\) m/s and acceleration \(a(t)=18-6t\) m/s². At which stop does it start moving to the left, and what is its acceleration there?
why: At \(4\) s the velocity changes from positive to negative. Substitution gives \(18-6(4)=-6\) m/s².

prompt: For \(y=3x-x^2\), the secant slope from \(x=1\) to \(x=b\) is \(2-b\) when \(b\ne1\). Which \(b\) makes the secant parallel to \(y=5-2x\)?
why: The secant slope from \(1\) to \(b\) simplifies to \(2-b\). Equating it to \(-2\) gives \(b=4\).

prompt: The parabola \(y=3x-x^2\) crosses the horizontal axis at \(0\) and \(3\). Its vertex is at \(x=3/2\). How far above the secant through the intercepts is the parallel tangent?
why: The secant is \(y=0\). A parallel tangent has \(3-2x=0\), hence height \(3(3/2)-(3/2)^2=9/4\).
Factor \(x^2-9=(x-3)(x+3)\). The first quotient tends to \(f'(3)=-2\), then divide by the limit \(6\).

prompt: Suppose \(f'(a)=3\). What is \(\lim_{h\to0}[f(a+h^2)-f(a)]/h\)?
why: Write it as \(h\) times the difference quotient with increment \(h^2\). The quotient tends to \(3\) and \(h\) tends to zero.

prompt: For \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+5}\), compare the slopes of the left secant (\(x=3\) to \(4\)), the tangent at \(4\), and the right secant (\(x=4\) to \(5\)). Which ordering holds?
why: Rationalizing gives slopes \(1/(3+\sqrt8)\) and \(1/(3+\sqrt{10})\). Their denominators lie on opposite sides of \(6\).

prompt: Use the derivative definition for \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+5}\) at its left endpoint \(x=-5\). What happens to its right-hand secant slopes?
choices: They increase without bound as the second point approaches \(-5\).
why: At an increment \(h>0\) the slope is \(\sqrt h/h=1/\sqrt h\). This grows without bound, giving a vertical endpoint tangent.

prompt: For \(g(x)=x\lvert x\rvert\), why does \(g'(0)\) exist even though the absolute-value factor has a corner?
choices: Its difference quotient at zero equals \(\lvert h\rvert\) and tends to zero.
The left and right slopes are \(-1\) and \(1\).
Every product of continuous functions is differentiable.
The difference quotient equals \(\lvert h\rvert/h\) and tends to one.
why: Since \(g(0)=0\), the quotient is \(h\lvert h\rvert/h\). Cancel the nonzero increment before taking its limit.

prompt: At \((4,3)\), the graph \(y=\sqrt{x+5}\) has tangent slope \(1/6\). Write that tangent as \(y=mx+b\). What is \(m+b\)?
why: The conjugate calculation gives \(m=1/6\). Since the line contains \((4,3)\), its intercept is \(7/3\), yielding \(m+b=15/6\).

prompt: A polynomial \(g\) satisfies \(g''(x)=-2\) everywhere and \(g(0)=0\). Which additional condition determines that \(g(x)=3x-x^2\) for every \(x\)?
why: A polynomial with second derivative \(-2\) and zero constant term has the form \(-x^2+bx\). Its first derivative at zero determines \(b\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=3x-x^2\), where do the graphs of \(f'\) and \(f''\) intersect?
why: Set \(3-2x=-2\) to find \(x=5/2\). Both derivative graphs have height \(-2\) there.

prompt: For \(f(x)=3x-x^2\), which equation finds every input where the height of the graph equals the tangent slope?
why: Set \(3x-x^2=3-2x\) and collect terms. This gives \(x^2-5x+3=0\).

prompt: If \(f\) is differentiable at \(a\) and \(f(a)\ne0\), find \(\lim_{h\to0}[1/f(a+h)-1/f(a)]/h\).
why: A common denominator gives the negative difference quotient of \(f\) divided by \(f(a+h)f(a)\). By continuity the latter tends to \(f(a)^2\ne0\).
Write the expression as \([f(h)/h][g(h)/h]\). Each bracket is a difference quotient at zero, so the limits multiply.

prompt: Consider \(f(x)=(x+1)^2\) for \(x\ne-1\) and \(f(-1)=1\). At which inputs \(a\) is \(f'(a)=0\)?
why: Away from \(-1\) the derivative is \(2(x+1)\), which has no zero there. At \(-1\) the jump between the assigned height and the limiting height prevents differentiability.

prompt: For \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+6}\), find an input where its tangent is perpendicular to a line of slope \(-4\).
why: The desired slope is \(1/4\). The derivative \(1/(2\sqrt{x+6})\) equals \(1/4\) precisely when \(x+6=4\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+6}\), the tangent at \(x=3\) estimates \(f(3+h)\) by \(3+h/6\). When \(h=7\), by how much does that estimate exceed the exact value?
why: At \(x=10\) the tangent estimate is \(25/6\) and the exact function value is \(4\). Their difference is \(1/6\).

prompt: On \(0\le t\le4\), a particle has velocity \(v(t)=3(t-2)^2-3\). Which list gives every time its speed reaches its maximum?
why: Velocity is \(3(t-2)^2-3\). Its range on the interval is \([-3,9]\), so the largest speed is \(9\) at the endpoints.

prompt: A particle starts at position \(0\), moves to \(9/4\) meters without reversing, then returns directly to \(0\). Compare its total distance and the magnitude of its displacement.
choices: Distance is \(9/2\) m and displacement is \(0\) m.
Distance is \(9/4\) m and displacement is \(0\) m.
Distance and displacement are both \(9/2\) m.
why: The two legs each cover \(9/4\) meters, giving \(9/2\) meters altogether. Initial and final positions coincide, so displacement is zero.

prompt: A car has position \(s(t)=(t-1)^2-4\) for \(t\ge0\). Which set contains exactly the positions it visits twice?
why: Rewrite as \(s=(t-1)^2-4\). Distinct times are \(1\pm\sqrt{s+4}\). Both are nonnegative exactly when \(0<s+4\le1\).

prompt: A ball has height \(H(t)=96-16t-16t^2\) feet. It falls from \(36\) ft at \(t=1.5\) s to ground at \(t=2\) s. What is its signed average velocity over this last half second?
why: Divide the signed displacement by the time: \((0-36)/(2-1.5)=-72\) ft/s.

prompt: A particle starts at \(5\) m, turns at \(-15\) m at \(t=2\) s, and next turns at \(-11\) m at \(t=4\) s. Which pair gives average velocity and average speed over the first four seconds, in m/s?
why: Displacement is \(-11-5=-16\) m. Distance is \(20+4=24\) m. Divide each by \(4\) s.

prompt: The tangent to \(y=1/x\) at \(x=a>0\) cuts the axes at \((2a,0)\) and \((0,2/a)\). If \(a\) doubles, how does the area enclosed by the tangent and the coordinate axes change?
why: Its base doubles and its height halves. Their product remains 4, so one half of the product remains 2.

prompt: Fish population \(P\) is measured in thousands, and \(t\) in years. What does \(P'(10)=2\) say?
choices: At year 10 the population is growing at 2,000 fish per year.
Exactly 2,000 fish were added between years 9 and 10.
why: The derivative is an instantaneous rate. The population unit contributes the factor of 1,000 and the time unit supplies “per year.”

prompt: Which tangent slope is represented by \(\lim_{x\to2}(x^3-8)/(x-2)\)?
choices: The slope of \(y=x^3\) at \(x=2\), equal to 12.
The slope of \(y=x^3\) at \(x=8\), equal to 192.
The slope of \(y=x^2\) at \(x=2\), equal to 4.
The slope of \(y=x^3\) at \(x=2\), equal to 8.
why: Match \(x^3-8\) with \(f(x)-f(2)\). The derivative of the cube is \(3x^2\), so the slope is 12.

prompt: A cart has velocity \(v(t)=3(t-2)(t-4)\) on \(0\le t\le6\). When does it reverse direction?
why: Each distinct linear factor changes sign at its zero. Velocity goes from positive to negative at 2, then from negative to positive at 4.

prompt: The graph shows \(f(x)=3x-x^2\), a downward-opening parabola with its peak at \(x=1.5\). Which graph shows \(f'\)?
choices: Falling line crossing the vertical axis at 3 and the horizontal axis at 1.5.
Rising line crossing the vertical axis at −3 and the horizontal axis at 1.5.
Horizontal line two units below the x-axis.
Falling line through the origin with slope −2.
why: The arch has a horizontal tangent at \(x=3/2\). Its slopes change from positive to negative. For the lecture curve \(f(x)=3x-x^2\), the derivative is \(3-2x\).

prompt: The line below is the derivative \(f'(x)=3-2x\). Which graph represents \(f''\)?
choices: Horizontal line two units below the x-axis.
Horizontal line two units above the x-axis.
Falling line through the origin with slope −2.
why: The line \(f'(x)=3-2x\) falls by two units for each unit step to the right. Its slope is always \(-2\).

prompt: The picture shows \(f(x)=|x|\). Which graph gives its derivative on the domain where the derivative exists?
choices: Horizontal ray at −1 on the left and at 1 on the right, both open at x = 0.
Horizontal ray at 1 on the left and at −1 on the right, both open at x = 0.
Two straight rays meet at a V-shaped corner at the origin.
Rising line through the origin and (1, 1).
why: The slope is \(-1\) for \(x<0\) and \(1\) for \(x>0\). The corner at zero has unequal one-sided slopes.

prompt: A particle has velocity \(v(t)=3-2t\) for \(0\le t\le3\). Which graph shows its speed?
choices: A V starts at height 3, touches zero at t = 1.5, and ends at height 3.
A falling line starts at height 3 and ends at −3.
A rising line starts at −3 and ends at 3.
An arch starts and ends at zero, with its peak at t = 1.5.
why: Speed is \(|v(t)|\). The negative part of the velocity line reflects above the horizontal axis after \(t=3/2\).

prompt: The position graph rises until \(t=1\), falls until \(t=3\), then rises again. The position is \(s(t)=t^3-6t^2+9t+2\) for \(0\le t\le4\). Which graph is the velocity?
choices: An upward parabola with zeros at 1 and 3 and a low point at (2, −3).
A downward parabola with zeros at 1 and 3 and a high point at (2, 3).
A curve rising to (1, 6), falling to (3, 2), then rising again.
A rising line crossing the horizontal axis at 2.
why: The particle stops at times 1 and 3. Its position rises, falls, then rises, so velocity has signs \(+, -, +\). The lecture model gives \(v(t)=3(t-1)(t-3)\).

prompt: The velocity graph is an upward-opening parabola with its minimum at \(t=2\). Which graph shows the acceleration?
choices: A rising line crossing the horizontal axis at 2.
An upward parabola with zeros at 1 and 3 and a low point at (2, −3).
A curve rising to (1, 6), falling to (3, 2), then rising again.
A downward parabola with zeros at 1 and 3 and a high point at (2, 3).
why: The parabola has negative slopes before 2, slope zero at 2, and positive slopes afterward. Differentiating \(3(t-1)(t-3)\) gives the line \(6(t-2)\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+5}\), the secant slope between inputs \(-1\) and \(-1+h\) is \(m(h)=1/(\sqrt{4+h}+2)\). What is the tangent slope at \(-1\) of \(g(x)=8f(x)-x\)?
why: As \(h\) tends to zero the secant slope tends to \(1/4\). Thus \(g'(-1)=8(1/4)-1=1\).

prompt: A point on \(y=\sqrt{x+5}\) has height \(u>0\) and tangent slope \(1/(2u)\). The tangent there has slope \(1/8\). Find the input \(x\) at that point.
why: The slope condition gives \(u=4\). Since \(u^2=x+5\), the input is \(16-5=11\).

prompt: For \(y=\sqrt{x+5}\), a secant joins the point \((4,3)\) to another point of height \(5\). Its slope is \(1/(3+5)\). What is the horizontal distance between these points?
why: The vertical change is \(5-3=2\). Since rise divided by run is \(1/8\), the horizontal change is \(16\).

prompt: Let \(F(x)=\lvert x\rvert[(x-2)^2+k]+3x\). Near zero, the factor in brackets tends to \(4+k\). Which \(k\) makes the left and right derivatives at zero agree?
why: The difference quotient at zero is \((\lvert h\rvert/h)[(h-2)^2+k]+3\). Its right and left limits are \(3+(4+k)\) and \(3-(4+k)\). Equality requires \(4+k=0\).

prompt: On \(y=3x-x^2\), the tangents at \(x=-1\) and \(x=3\) have equations \(y=5x+1\) and \(y=-3x+9\). What is the height of their intersection?
why: The tangent at \(a\) is \(y=(3-2a)x+a^2\). The two lines are \(y=5x+1\) and \(y=-3x+9\). They intersect at \(x=1\) and hence \(y=6\).

prompt: On \(y=3x-x^2\), the tangents through \((2,3)\) touch at \(x=1\) and \(x=3\). What is the product of their slopes?
why: The line tangent at \(a\) has equation \(y=(3-2a)x+a^2\). Passing through \((2,3)\) requires \(a^2-4a+3=0\), so \(a=1,3\). Their slopes are \(1,-3\).

prompt: Suppose \(f'(a)=-3/2\). As \(h\to0\), what is the limit of \([f(a+3h)-f(a-h)]/h\)?
why: Insert \(f(a)\) between the two terms. The forward change divided by \(h\) tends to \(3f'(a)\) and the backward change contributes \(f'(a)\). Together they give \(4(-3/2)=-6\).

prompt: Let \(f(2)=4\) and \(f'(2)=3\). The denominator factors as \(x^2-4=(x-2)(x+2)\). Find \(\lim_{x\to2}(\sqrt{f(x)}-2)/(x^2-4)\).
why: Rationalize the numerator and factor the denominator. The expression becomes the difference quotient \([f(x)-4]/(x-2)\) divided by \((\sqrt{f(x)}+2)(x+2)\). The respective limits are \(3\) and \(16\).

prompt: Let \(f(x)=3x-x^2\) and \(g(x)=f(2x)\). The graph of \(f'\) is a line of slope \(-2\). What is the slope of the graph of \(g'\)?
why: Applying the chain rule twice gives \(g''(x)=4f''(2x)=4(-2)=-8\).
The linear term contributes zero to the second derivative. Hence \(q''(x)=6x-2\), giving \(10\) at \(x=2\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=3x-x^2\), let \(G(x)=f(x)-f'(x)\). At what input does the graph of \(G\) have a horizontal tangent?
why: The slope of \(G\) is \(f'-f''=(3-2x)-(-2)=5-2x\). This vanishes at \(5/2\).

prompt: Let \(f(x)=(x+1)^2\) for \(x\le-1\) and \(f(x)=A(x+1)^2+B(x+1)\) for \(x>-1\). If \(f\) is twice differentiable at \(-1\), find \(A+B\).
why: The left slope is zero, so the right slope at the join forces \(B=0\). Matching the second derivatives gives \(2=2A\), hence \(A=1\).

prompt: For \(x\ne-1\), set \(f(x)=(x^3+3x^2+3x+1)/(x+1)\). Assign the unique value at \(x=-1\) that makes \(f\) continuous. What is \(f''(-1)\) for this repaired function?
why: The numerator factors as \((x+1)^3\), so nearby values equal \((x+1)^2\). Continuity forces the missing value to be zero. The repaired function equals the quadratic everywhere, whose second derivative is \(2\).
Combine the fractions and insert \(2h\) as the derivative increment. The limit is \(-2f'(0)/(2f(0))\). Substitute \(f'(0)=-3\) and \(f(0)=2\).
The first factor divided by \(h\) tends to \(2f'(1)=-4\). The second divided by \(h\) tends to \(-3g'(1)=-9\). Multiplication gives \(36\).

prompt: Let \(F(x)=x\lvert x\rvert\). Its first derivative is \(2\lvert x\rvert\), including at zero. Find the right-hand slope of \(F'\) at zero minus its left-hand slope.
why: For positive \(x\), \(F'=2x\) has slope \(2\). For negative \(x\), \(F'=-2x\) has slope \(-2\). The difference is \(4\).

prompt: On \((1,2)\) and \((3,4)\), a particle speeds up without reversing. These are its only speeding-up intervals. Its positions at times \(1,2,3,4\) are \(6,4,2,6\) meters, respectively. How many meters does it travel while speeding up?
why: From time \(1\) to \(2\), the particle covers \(2\) meters. From \(3\) to \(4\), it covers \(4\) meters. The two distances sum to \(6\).

prompt: A particle has velocity \(v(t)=3-2t\) m/s for \(0\le t\le3\). For what fraction of these three seconds is its speed greater than \(2\) m/s?
why: The speed exceeds \(2\) for the first and the last half second. Those periods total \(1\) of the \(3\) seconds.

prompt: A ball’s velocity is \(v(t)=-16-32t\) ft/s from release until impact. Its impact speed is \(80\) ft/s. How many seconds after release is its downward speed half its impact speed?
why: Half the impact speed is \(40\), so the velocity must be \(-40\). Solving \(-16-32t=-40\) gives \(t=24/32=3/4\).

prompt: A ball drops from \(96\) ft to ground level in \(2\) seconds. Its velocity is \(v(t)=-16-32t\) ft/s. At what time does its velocity equal its average velocity over the flight? Enter seconds.
why: The average velocity is \(-96/2=-48\). Solving \(-16-32t=-48\) gives \(t=1\).

prompt: A car starts at position \(-3\) ft and reaches \(5\) ft. It reverses exactly once along the way, at the minimum of \(s(t)=(t-1)^2-4\). How many feet does it travel?
why: It reverses at \(t=1\), where \(s=-4\), and reaches \(s=5\) at \(t=4\). The trip starts at \(s=-3\), so the two legs have lengths \(1\) and \(9\).

prompt: A particle starts at \(5\) m, reverses at \(-15\) m, reverses again at \(-11\) m, and ends at \(-15\) m. There are no other reversals. The trip lasts \(5\) s. What is its average speed in m/s?
why: The three legs cover \(20\), \(4\) and \(4\) meters. Divide total distance by elapsed time to get \(28/5\) m/s.

prompt: On \(0<t<5\), a particle has \(v=-3(t-2)(t-4)\) and \(a=6(3-t)\). Its positions at \(t=4\) and \(5\) are \(-11\) and \(-15\) meters. How far does it travel while both \(v\) and \(a\) are negative?
why: Velocity is negative before \(2\) and after \(4\). Acceleration \(18-6t\) is negative after \(3\). Their negative signs coincide on \((4,5)\), during which position drops from \(-11\) to \(-15\), a distance of \(4\).

prompt: A particle first reverses at position \(-15\) m. Its position satisfies \(s(t)+15=-(t-2)^2(t-5)\), and its velocity is \(v(t)=-3(t-2)(t-4)\) m/s. What is its speed when it returns to \(-15\) m after the reversal?
why: The first reversal is at \(t=2\), where \(s=-15\). Solving \(s(t)+15=-(t-2)^2(t-5)=0\) gives the later time \(5\). The velocity \(-3(t-2)(t-4)\) is then \(-9\).

prompt: On \(y=\sqrt{x+5}\), two points are \(P=(-4,1)\) and \(Q=(11,4)\). At a point of height \(u\), the tangent slope is \(1/(2u)\). What is the height where the tangent is parallel to secant \(PQ\)?
At \(x=3\), join the left branch \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+6}\) to the right branch \(A+B(x-3)\). The graph must be differentiable at the join. Find \(A\cdot B\).
why: The branches must agree in value and slope. The left value is \(3\) and its derivative there is \(1/(2\sqrt9)=1/6\). Thus \(A=3\), \(B=1/6\), and \(AB=1/2\).

prompt: Two runners meet at \(t=1\) and again at \(t=4\). Between these meetings, the first runner moves from \(6\) m to \(2\) m and back to \(6\) m, reversing only at \(2\) m. What is this runner’s average speed between the meetings, in m/s?
why: The runner covers \(4+4=8\) meters in \(4-1=3\) seconds. Its average speed is \(8/3\) m/s even though its displacement is zero.

prompt: A cart travels from \(0\) m at \(t=0\) s to \(36\) m at \(t=6\) s. Its velocity is \(v(t)=3(t-2)(t-4)\) m/s. Which pair gives its average velocity on \([0,6]\) and its final velocity, in m/s?
why: The displacement is \(s(6)-s(0)=36\) m, so its average over 6 s is 6 m/s. Substituting 6 into \(3t^2-18t+24\) gives 24 m/s.

prompt: A cart starts at \(0\) m and first reverses at \(20\) m. It next reverses at \(16\) m and finishes at \(36\) m. There are no other reversals. How many meters did it travel?
why: The three distances are \(20-0=20\), \(20-16=4\) and \(36-16=20\) meters. Their sum is \(44\).

prompt: A tangent line rises 2 units for each unit to the right. What is the derivative at the point of contact?
why: The tangent slope is the rise divided by the run.

prompt: The graph shown is a horizontal line. What is its derivative at the origin?
why: The height stays constant as the input changes.

prompt: The graph is a rising straight line. Is its tangent slope positive, negative, zero, or undefined?
why: Moving to the right increases the height.

prompt: The graph shown is a falling straight line. What sign does its derivative have?
why: The line loses height as the input increases.

prompt: The curve has a smooth lowest point at the origin. What is its tangent slope there?
why: The tangent at the bottom of the bowl is horizontal.

prompt: Two rays meet in a sharp V at the origin. Does the graph have a derivative there?
why: The left ray falls and the right ray rises.

prompt: If \(f'(2)=5\), what is the slope of the tangent to \(y=f(x)\) at \(x=2\)?
why: The derivative is the tangent slope.

prompt: The marked point of tangency is \((1,1)\). The dashed tangent also passes through \((2,3)\). What is its slope?
why: The rise is 2 and the run is 1.

prompt: A secant changes height by \(6\) while the horizontal input changes by \(3\). What is its slope?
why: Divide the vertical change by the horizontal change.

prompt: In \([f(a+h)-f(a)]/h\), which symbol measures the change in input?
why: The two inputs differ by \(h\).

prompt: What is the name for the straight line determined by two points of a graph at different inputs?
why: The secant slope compares the two points.

prompt: For \(f(x)=3x+4\), what is the instantaneous slope at \(x=0\)?
why: A straight line has the same slope everywhere.

prompt: The derivative function is \(f'(x)=2x\). What is \(f'(1)\)?
why: Substitute \(x=1\).

prompt: The graph shown is \(f'\). What sign does the tangent slope of \(f\) have at \(x=1\)?
why: The derivative graph is above the horizontal axis at that input.

prompt: The graph shown is \(f'\). What is \(f'(0)\)?
why: The entire graph lies at height \(-2\).

prompt: The graph shown is \(f'\). What is the tangent slope of \(f\) at \(x=0\)?
why: Read the height at the origin.

prompt: If \(f'(x)=6\) for all \(x\), what is \(f''(x)\)?
why: A constant has zero derivative.

prompt: Which symbol means the second derivative of \(y\) with respect to \(x\)?
why: The 2 on the differential notation counts derivatives.

prompt: Start with \(f\). How many times do you differentiate to obtain \(f''\)?
why: Each prime records one derivative.

prompt: Given \(f'(x)=3-2x\), what is the derivative value at \(x=0\)?
why: At zero the term \(-2x\) vanishes.

prompt: A graph has a sharp corner where the one-sided slopes differ. What happens to its derivative at the corner?
choices: It equals the height of the corner.
why: A derivative requires a single limiting slope.

prompt: The slope of \(f\) at \(x=4\) is \(-1\). Which point on the derivative graph records this particular slope?
why: On the derivative graph the height is the slope of the original function.

prompt: If \(f'(x)=-1\) for every \(x\), what is \(f'(8)\)?
why: The derivative has the same value at every input.
Use \(-2\) as the input to the derivative function.

prompt: A particle moves along a number line with velocity \(-2\) m/s. While its velocity stays negative, how does its position change?
why: A negative velocity indicates motion in the negative direction.

prompt: A particle is momentarily at rest. What is its instantaneous velocity in m/s?
why: Being at rest means its instantaneous velocity is zero.

prompt: If \(s(t)\) is position, what is \(s'(t)\)?
why: Velocity is the derivative of position.

prompt: If \(v(t)\) is velocity, what is \(v'(t)\)?
why: Acceleration measures how fast velocity changes.

prompt: A car has velocity \(4\) m/s. What is its speed in m/s?
why: Speed is the magnitude of velocity.

prompt: Position is measured in meters and time in seconds. What are the units of velocity?
why: Velocity is change in position per unit time.

prompt: A particle moves at a constant velocity. What is its acceleration in m/s²?
why: Constant velocity has zero rate of change.

prompt: Which quantity is always nonnegative for motion along a line?
why: Speed is the absolute value of velocity.

prompt: The graph shows velocity in m/s. What is the speed when the graph crosses the time axis?
why: At the crossing, velocity and its absolute value are both zero.

prompt: The graph shows position. What sign does the velocity have at \(t=1\)?
why: The position graph is rising at this instant.

prompt: The vertical coordinate is velocity in m/s. Read the velocity at \(t=0\) from the graph.
why: Read the vertical intercept at time zero.

prompt: A ball is falling toward the ground. Height is measured upward. What sign does its vertical velocity have?
why: The height is decreasing with time.

prompt: The graph shows position in meters against time in seconds. What is the instantaneous velocity at the smooth peak, in m/s?
why: The tangent to position is horizontal at the peak.

prompt: The secant slope for \(f\) from \(2\) to \(2+h\) simplifies to \(3+h\) when \(h\ne0\). What is \(f'(2)\)?
why: Take the limit of the secant slopes as \(h\) approaches zero.

prompt: For \(f(x)=\lvert x\rvert\), the secant from the origin to a point with \(x=h<0\) has what slope?
why: On the left ray, \(\lvert h\rvert=-h\), so the slope \(\lvert h\rvert/h\) equals \(-1\).

prompt: The secant slope for \(f\) from \(4\) to \(4+h\) simplifies to \(1+h\) when \(h\ne0\). What is \(f'(4)\)?
why: Take the limit of the secant slopes as \(h\) approaches zero.

prompt: The tangent passes through \((1,3)\) with slope \(2\). On this tangent, what is the height one unit to the right?
why: One unit of run changes height by \(2\). Start from \(3\).

prompt: The tangent passes through \((2,5)\) with slope \(-1\). On this tangent, what is the height one unit to the right?
why: One unit of run changes height by \(-1\). Start from \(5\).

prompt: A tangent has equation \(y-2=3(x-1)\). At which input does it reach height \(5\)?
why: The line rises by \(3\) when the input increases from \(1\) to \(2\).

prompt: The secant through \((1,3)\) and \((3,7)\) has what slope?
why: Divide the vertical change \(4\) by the horizontal change \(2\).

prompt: The secant through \((-1,2)\) and \((1,0)\) has what slope?
why: Divide the vertical change \(-2\) by the horizontal change \(2\).

prompt: The graph is \(|x|\). On its left branch, what slope do all the secants have?
why: The graph is a line of slope minus one throughout that branch.

prompt: The graph of \(f\) is a smooth bowl. How does the sign of the tangent slope change as you pass through the bottom from left to right?
why: The graph first descends and then ascends.

prompt: The second derivative is \(f''(x)=3x\). What is its value at \(x=2\)?
why: Substitute the requested input in the second derivative.

prompt: The graph shows \(f'\). Where is \(f\) increasing within the displayed interval?
choices: To the right of the origin
To the left of the origin
On both sides of the origin
On neither side of the origin
why: The graph of the derivative is positive precisely on the right side.

prompt: A graph has \(f''(x)=5x\). At which input does the slope of the graph of \(f'\) equal \(-5\)?
why: The slope of the derivative graph is \(f''(x)\). Solve \(5x=-5\).
Differentiating gives \(2x+2\), whose value at zero is \(2\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=3x-x^2\), \(f'(x)=3-2x\). Which equation gives the graph of \(f''\)?
why: The slope of the line \(3-2x\) is the same at every input.

prompt: On a whole interval, \(f'(x)=5\). What happens to the tangent slopes of \(f\) as you move from left to right?
choices: They start at 5 and steadily increase.
why: The constant derivative means that every tangent on the interval has slope 5.

prompt: The graph is \(f'\), a falling line. What is the sign of \(f''\)?
why: The slope of the derivative graph is negative.

prompt: The graph shows \(f'\). At \(x=2\), what is the sign of the tangent slope of \(f\)?
why: The derivative graph is below the horizontal axis at input 2.

prompt: On a straight track, \(v(t)=2t-1\) m/s. What is the speed at \(t=1\) s, in m/s?
why: Substitute the time and take the absolute value of the velocity.

prompt: On a straight track, \(v(t)=3t-1\) m/s. What is the speed at \(t=2\) seconds in m/s?
why: Substitute the time and take the absolute value of the velocity.

prompt: A cart moves from position \(2\) m to \(5\) m in one second. What is its signed average velocity in m/s?
why: Subtract the starting position from the ending position and divide by one second.

prompt: A cart moves from position \(3\) m to \(1\) m in one second. What is its signed average velocity in m/s?
why: Subtract the starting position from the ending position and divide by one second.

prompt: The graph shows position against time. Between the smooth peak and the right endpoint, what is the sign of the velocity?
why: The position curve has negative slope throughout this interval.

prompt: The graph shows a velocity that drops through zero. How does the direction of travel change?
why: The velocity starts above the time axis and ends below it.

prompt: A differentiable \(f\) satisfies \(f(2)=1\), \(f'(2)=3\). What is \(\lim_{h\to0}[f(2+2h)-f(2)]/h\)?
why: The actual input increment is \(2h\). Writing \(h=(2h)/2\) gives twice the derivative.

prompt: For \(y=x^2\), the secant through inputs \(1\) and \(3\) has slope \(4\). At what input does the parabola have a parallel tangent?
why: Set the tangent slope \(2x\) equal to the secant slope.

prompt: The graph is \(f'(x)=3-2x\). If \(g(x)=f(x)+x\), at which input does \(g\) have a horizontal tangent?
why: Adding \(x\) raises each derivative value by one. Solve \(4-2x=0\).

prompt: A function has \(f'(x)=2x\). What is the second derivative at zero of \(g(x)=f(x)-x^2\)?
why: The derivative of \(g\) is \(2x-2x=0\) everywhere.

prompt: For \(y=x^2\), the secant through inputs \(a\) and \(a+2\) has slope \(2a+2\). It is parallel to a tangent of slope 8 at \(x=4\). Find \(a\).
why: The tangent slope is 8. Solving \(2a+2=8\) gives \(a=3\).

prompt: \(f\) is differentiable at \(1\) with \(f'(1)=-2\). Evaluate \(\lim_{h\to0}[f(1+3h)-f(1)]/(2h)\).
why: The denominator is \(2/3\) of the input change \(3h\). The limit is \((3/2)f'(1)\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=x^2\), two tangents are drawn at inputs \(1\) and \(3\). Their slopes are \(2\) and \(6\). What is the horizontal coordinate of their intersection?
why: Their equations are \(y=2x-1\) and \(y=6x-9\). Set the right sides equal.

prompt: A function equals \(x^2\) for \(x\le1\) and \(mx+b\) for \(x>1\). Choose \(m,b\) so that it is differentiable at \(1\). What is \(b\)?
why: Matching slopes gives \(m=2\). Matching heights then requires \(2+b=1\).

prompt: The secant slope of \(f(x)=3x-x^2\) between distinct inputs \(a,b\) equals \(3-a-b\). A secant from \(a=0\) is parallel to the tangent of slope 1 at \(x=1\). What is \(b\)?
why: The tangent has slope \(3-2(1)=1\). Solve \(3-b=1\).

prompt: For \(x>0\) let \(f(x)=1/x\). Its tangent at \(x=2\) has slope \(-1/4\). At what input does this tangent meet the horizontal axis?
For a differentiable function, \(f'(4)=3\). Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to4}[f(x)-f(4)]/(x^2-16)\).
why: Factor the denominator. The difference quotient approaches 3, and its other divisor approaches 8.

prompt: \(f'(x)=2x-1\). For \(g(x)=f(x)+f'(x)\), at which input is \(g'=0\)?
Let \(g(x)=f(x)+f(-x)\) for a twice differentiable \(f\) with \(f''(0)=3\). What is \(g''(0)\)?
why: Differentiating the reflected term twice introduces two minus signs. Add the two second derivatives at zero.

prompt: The derivative graph of \(f\) is the falling line \(f'(x)=3-2x\). For \(g(x)=2f(x)-x\), at which input is its tangent horizontal?
why: \(g'=2(3-2x)-1\). Set this equal to zero.

prompt: The derivative of \(f\) is \(f'(x)=x^2-1\). What is the difference \(f''(2)-f'(2)\)?
why: At \(2\), the second derivative \(2x\) equals 4, while the first derivative equals 3.

prompt: For some \(a\), the graph of \(f'\) has tangent line \(y=3x-2\) at \(x=a\). If \(f'(a)=4\), what is \(a+f''(a)\)?
why: The tangency point satisfies \(4=3a-2\), so \(a=2\). The slope of the derivative graph is 3.

prompt: Let \(f(x)=x^2\) when \(x\ge0\) and \(f(x)=kx^2\) when \(x<0\). The derivative at zero is zero. For \(f''(0)\) to exist, what must \(k\) equal?
why: The one-sided slopes of the derivative are \(2\) and \(2k\) and must agree.

prompt: Two twice differentiable functions have the same tangent line at \(x=1\). If \(f''(1)=5\) and \(g''(1)=2\), what is \(\lim_{h\to0}[f'(1+h)-g'(1+h)]/h\)?
why: Their first derivatives agree at 1. The limit is the derivative of \(f'-g'\) there.

prompt: A cart on a straight track moves forward on \(0<t<1\) and backward on \(1<t<3\). At times \(0,1,3\) seconds its positions are \(0,4,1\) meters. What is the average speed over the full three seconds in m/s?
why: It travels 4 meters forward and 3 back. Divide 7 by the 3-second duration.

prompt: Two cars move along one track. Their positions are \(s_A=t^2\) and \(s_B=3t\) in meters. At their meeting with \(t>0\), what is \(v_A-v_B\) in m/s?
why: The positive meeting time is 3 seconds. There the velocities are 6 and 3 m/s.

prompt: A particle has \(s(t)=3t-t^2\) m and turns at \(t=3/2\) s. What distance in meters does it travel from \(t=1\) to \(t=2\)?
why: Its endpoint positions are both 2 m. The maximum is \(9/4\) m, so it travels \(1/4\) m each way.

prompt: The velocity is \(v(t)=3-2t\) m/s. A cart travels forward and later backward at the same speed of 1 m/s. How many seconds separate those two instants?
why: Solve \(3-2t=1\) and \(3-2t=-1\). The times are 1 and 2.

prompt: A ball has height \(H(t)=96-16t-16t^2\) feet and hits the ground at \(t=2\) s. How much greater is its impact speed than its initial speed, in ft/s?
why: The velocity is \(-16-32t\). The speeds are 16 at launch and 80 at impact.

prompt: A cart moves forward until \(t=2\) s, then backward through \(t=5\) s. Its positions at \(0,2,5\) seconds are \(-2,4,1\) meters. Over all five seconds, by how much does average speed exceed the magnitude of average velocity, in m/s?
why: Distance is \(6+3=9\) m and displacement is \(3\) m. Divide their difference by 5 seconds.

prompt: Which graph shows a line with positive tangent slope everywhere?
choices: Rising line through the origin and (1, 2).
Falling line through the origin and (1, −2).
Smooth U-shaped curve with its lowest point at the origin.
Two straight rays meet at a V-shaped corner at the origin.
why: Only the rising straight line has positive slope at every input.

prompt: The plotted curve is \(f(x)=x^2\). Which graph gives the slope \(f'(x)\)?
choices: Rising line through the origin and (1, 2).
Falling line through the origin and (1, −2).
Smooth U-shaped curve with its lowest point at the origin.
Two straight rays meet at a V-shaped corner at the origin.
why: The slope is negative on the left, zero at the bottom, and positive on the right. Its formula is \(2x\).

prompt: The graph gives speed on a straight track. The particle starts by moving forward, stops once, then moves backward. Which velocity graph fits?
choices: A falling line starts at height 3 and ends at −3.
A rising line starts at −3 and ends at 3.
A V starts at height 3, touches zero at t = 1.5, and ends at height 3.
An arch starts and ends at zero, with its peak at t = 1.5.
why: The velocity agrees with the speed before the stop and equals negative speed afterward.
